SOURCE: "HIRAG: Hierarchical-Thought Instruction-Tuning Retrieval-Augmented Generation", Yihan Jiao*, Zhehao Tan* (equal first authors), Dan Yang, Duolin Sun, Jie Feng, Yue Shen, Jian Wang, Peng Wei (AntGroup). arXiv:2507.05714v3, cs.CL, 10 Sep 2025. No venue is stated in the text, so call it a preprint. First author: Jiao.

COVERAGE: 20 of 20 pages and 42,591 of 42,591 chars of extracted text were read, including the references and appendices A.1, A.2 and B. Figures 3-13 are images (data-quality chart, train-data example, prompt templates), so their content is not in the extraction. Only their captions were read. I did not view the images.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Training on three progressive tasks (filtering, then combination, then RAG-specific reasoning), each with its own CoT format, beats the same-size baselines and prior RAG-tuned models.
 - number: HIRAG Llama3-8B scores 66.6 PopQA, 49.2 HotpotQA, 27.8 MuSiQue, 74.6 PubMedQA EM, 94.6 RGB-noise, 66.0 RGB-int.
 - setup: Zero-shot, accuracy except PubMedQA, which is EM. Contriever-MS retriever, vLLM inference. The documents are fixed per dataset (top-10 for HotpotQA and MuSiQue). Baselines used public weights and prompts.
 - quote: "HIRAG(Llama3-8B) 94.6 66.0 66.6 49.2 27.8 74.6"
 - where: Table 1, p.7
2. The paper states its gain over the best prior RAG-specific model in percentage points.
 - number: +2.5 PopQA, +2.4 HotpotQA, +7.7 MuSiQue.
 - setup: 8B model. The comparison is against the "current state-of-the-art" among the models in Table 1.
 - quote: "our model achieved substantial improvements of 2.5, 2.4, and 7.7 percentage points over the current state-of-the-art models on the PopQA, HotpotQA, and Musique datasets, respectively"
 - where: Section 4.2, p.7
3. The tuned 8B model does not beat the large models everywhere.
 - number: On PopQA, HIRAG-8B scores 66.6 against 67.2 for Llama3-70B-Instruct, and beats GPT-4 (63.3) and GPT-4o-mini (64.2). On PubMedQA, HIRAG-8B scores 74.6 against 65.4, 58.3 and 56.8 for those three. On HotpotQA, GPT-4o-mini scores 54.2 against 49.2. On MuSiQue, GPT-4o-mini scores 37.7 against 27.8. On RGB-noise, the large models score 98-99 against 94.6.
 - setup: Table 1, same as above.
 - quote: "GPT-4o-mini 99.0 86.0 64.2 54.2 37.7 56.8"
 - where: Table 1, p.7
4. Ablation: adding combination and reasoning data lifts RGB-int a lot and leaves RGB-noise about flat.
 - number: English, Llama3-8B. RGB-int goes from 48.0 at 1:0:0 to 58.0 at 1:1:0 and 66.0 at 1:2:2. RGB-noise stays at 94.3-96.6. Chinese, Qwen2.5-7B. RGB-int goes from 53.0 at 1:0:0 to 78.0 at 1:2:2.
 - setup: The total data amount is held constant and only the Filtering:Combination:Reasoning ratio changes. Chosen ratio is 1:2:2.
 - quote: "HIRAG1:0:0 94.3 48.0" and "HIRAG1:2:2 94.666.0"
 - where: Table 3, p.8. Table 4 (Chinese) p.9.
5. Chinese RGB results: a 7B model tuned with HIRAG approaches Qwen2.5-72B.
 - number: HIRAG(Qwen2.5-7B) scores 95.3 noise and 78.0 int. Qwen2.5-32B scores 89.7 and 77.0. Qwen2.5-72B scores 96.0 and 84.0. Untuned Qwen2.5-7B scores 86.3 and 71.0.
 - quote: "HIRAG(Qwen2.5-7B) 95.3 78.0"
 - where: Table 2, p.7
6. Training recipe and cost.
 - number: About 120K samples, 8 A100 GPUs, about 32 h (Llama3-8B) and about 28 h (Llama2-7B). Learning rate 3e-5, batch size 4, max length 4096. 20-30% of samples have their documents shuffled.
 - quote: "The training dataset, consisting of approximately 120K samples" and "shuffling the documents (20%-30% of all samples)"
 - where: Appendix A.1 and Section 3.3
7. The "think before answering" step costs a little extra inference time, and more for harder tasks.
 - number: Thinking time is 0.0860 s (filtering), 0.1199 s (combination) and 0.1427 s (reasoning). Average input is about 4.3-4.6K tokens.
 - setup: HIRAG-8B, 4 A100s, batch 64, vLLM greedy decoding at temperature 0.0, input lengths held equal.
 - quote: "Think Process Elapsed Time (s) 0.0860 0.1199 0.1427"
 - where: Table 5, Appendix A.2
8. Method details worth keeping.
 - The filtering CoT must use direct quotations (<quote>) and source citations (<cite>). The combination CoT names the relations between sources (parallel, hierarchical, inclusive). The reasoning CoT is an explicit reasoning chain.
 - The model uses <|REASON|> and <|ANSWER|> tokens, following RAFT.
 - Reasoning types are comparative, deductive and causal. "Implicit" reasoning mixes document facts with the model's internal knowledge.
 - Training data is synthesized by GPT-4-turbo, Qwen-MAX and GPT-4o from Wikipedia, HotpotQA and PubMedQA documents (QA parts not used). It is then verified for task-definition compliance and answer correctness (a GPT-4 answer is compared with the synthetic answer), and failing samples are dropped.
 - The same document with a different query gives a different task. A biography asked about "activities in a year" is filtering. Asked about "activities at a certain age", it needs reasoning.
 - where: Sections 3.1-3.3, Appendix A.1

LIMITS
- Authors concede heavy dependence on documents. In their words: "its performance declines when the documents only provide supplementary information without containing the exact answers."
- Authors also concede that general-knowledge RAG tuning is insufficient for specialized domains, and propose two-stage tuning as future work.
- Retrieval is fixed or uses Contriever-MS only. RGB is evaluated with fixed documents. No retriever ablation.
- No faithfulness or citation-accuracy metric is reported, even though the CoT uses <cite>. Only answer accuracy is measured.
- No head-to-head ablation of CoT against no-CoT is visible beyond the data-ratio tables. The 1:0:0 row is filtering-only with CoT. I saw no no-thought baseline.
- The authors manually corrected errors in RGB and give the corrected version only "upon request", so results are not exactly reproducible from the public RGB.
- Some Table 1 baseline numbers for RAFT and RankRAG are copied from their papers, not rerun. Cells marked "-" are missing.
- Small test sets (RGB-int numbers are in whole percentage steps), single runs, no variance reported.
- Dated: baselines are Llama2/3 era (Self-RAG, RQ-RAG, ChatQA). Reasoning-model RAG tuning (e.g. RL-trained) is not covered. The authors list RL as future work.

BUILDS ON
- Zhang et al. 2024, RAFT (arXiv:2403.10131): distractor documents, <|REASON|>/<|ANSWER|> tokens, CoT.
- Yu et al. 2024, RankRAG.
- Schimanski et al. 2024, EvidenceRAG.
- Wei et al. 2024, InstructRAG.
- Liu et al. 2024, ChatQA.
- Zhao et al. 2024, empirical study of RAG with CoT (arXiv:2407.15569).
- Wei et al. 2023, chain-of-thought.
- Asai et al. 2023b, Self-RAG.
- Chan et al. 2024, RQ-RAG.
- Chen et al. 2023, RGB benchmark.
- Gan et al. 2024, multi-layered thoughts (same AntGroup group).
- Eval datasets: Mallen et al. 2023 (PopQA), Yang et al. 2018 (HotpotQA), Trivedi et al. 2022 (MuSiQue), Jin et al. 2019 (PubMedQA).

CODE
- Evaluation prompt for the RAG benchmark (Table 6, Appendix B.2), verbatim: "You are an accurate and reliable AI assistant that can answer questions with the help of external documents. Please note that external documents may contain noisy or factually incorrect information. If the information in the document contains the correct answer, you will give an accurate answer. If the information in the document does not contain the answer, you will generate 'I can not answer the question because of the insufficient information in documents.' If there are inconsistencies with the facts in some of the documents, please generate the response 'There are factual errors in the provided documents.' and provide the correct answer."
- Data construction: Algorithm 1 (Appendix A.1). Task-specific query templates are in Figures 6-13, which are images and were not read.

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p.2: the three progressive capabilities. It explains the idea fastest.
- Fig 2, p.4: overview of training and inference. It shows the different "Thought" per task (filter, then combine, then reason). This is the best figure to reuse.
- Fig 3, p.6: data-quality verification results.
- Fig 4, p.8: MuSiQue case study, HIRAG-8B against Llama-8B-Instruct.
- Fig 5, p.12: a training example.
- Figs 6-13, pp.13-20: prompt templates.

TARGET NOTE (06-generation-for-rag.md)
- Strongest point: a RAG-tuned generator needs graded tasks (filter, combine, reason), and only the reasoning-heavy data moves multi-document integration. The 1:0:0 to 1:2:2 ablation (RGB-int 48 to 66) shows this. Filtering and distractor training alone, which is RAFT's recipe, leaves RGB-noise high but integration weak.
- Best section: "RAG vs fine-tuning" (note line 513), next to the RARE paragraph at line 522. It would also support "Hallucinations and citations" (line 315) through the <quote>/<cite> filtering CoT, though the paper does not measure citation quality.
- Does the note already say it? Not in the HIRAG sense. My grep for "RAFT" over the note returned no hit, so the claim that note 06 covers RAFT could not be confirmed. RARE is covered (line 522). Cuconasu et al. distractor findings are at lines 558 and 587. "HIRAG", "filtering", "instruction tuning" and "think before answering" do not appear in the note.
- Treat it as new content that extends the RARE sentence, with a caveat that HIRAG compares only against other tuned or prompted models and not against RAG with a non-tuned model of the same size beyond Table 1.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Figures 3-13 contain no extractable text. Minor extraction typos ("RAG-pecific", "Casual" in a caption), which are the paper's own typos.
